evals.prompt: I am a final-year engineering student in Pune. Build my first resume from these notes, but do not invent metrics. I know Java, Python, SQL, made a hostel maintenance ticketing project with three classmates, completed a six-week internship, and want an entry-level backend role. Ask only the questions needed to verify facts, then create DOCX and PDF.
evals.expected_output: A concise early-career resume plus a fact-check list, evidence record, editable DOCX, selectable PDF, and extraction report. No invented users, percentages, or business impact.
assertions: No unsupported metric or employer claim appears.
The output uses a one-column structure with standard headings.
DOCX and PDF text extraction preserve the material content.

evals.prompt: Tailor my attached senior operations resume to this program director posting. The posting asks for a $10M budget, but my verified maximum budget is $4.2M. Keep that gap honest, map every major requirement, and create interview questions from the final evidence.
evals.expected_output: A truthful targeted variant that retains the verified $4.2M scope, marks the $10M requirement as a gap or transferable evidence, and produces evidence-linked interview practice.
assertions: The resume never changes $4.2M to $10M.
Unsupported requirements are visible in the requirement matrix.
Interview answers cite verified resume evidence.

evals.prompt: Audit this visually fancy two-column PDF for ATS readability. Do not rewrite it yet. Tell me exactly what extracted, what was missing or out of order, and whether I should submit PDF or DOCX for the Greenhouse application instructions I pasted.
evals.expected_output: A diagnostic extraction report rather than a made-up ATS score, with the employer instructions controlling the format recommendation.
assertions: No predictive ATS score is given.
The report distinguishes observable extraction from uncertain vendor behavior.
The pasted application instructions override generic file advice.

evals.prompt: Create an academic CV for a postdoctoral application in Germany from my publications, teaching, grants, and research history. The university requests Europass-compatible information and explicitly asks for a photo.
evals.expected_output: An academic-CV workflow that follows the institution's explicit request, applies European context cautiously, and does not force a private-sector two-page limit.
assertions: The academic CV is not forced into one or two pages.
The explicit photo request is surfaced for informed confirmation.
Private-sector ATS conventions are not treated as universal.

evals.prompt: Start my resume from scratch. I am a registered nurse moving from a medical-surgical unit to emergency care. I am not sure which details matter, so guide me in short rounds and let me skip questions I cannot answer yet.
evals.expected_output: A resumable scratch intake routed to the clinical-healthcare domain, with no more than three questions per round and prompts for licensure, patient setting, clinical scope, safety, collaboration, and outcomes.
assertions: The first response asks no more than three questions.
The workflow distinguishes licensure from ordinary skills.
Unknown details remain open rather than being invented.

evals.prompt: Use my old electrician resume as the starting point. First show what you could extract, what is uncertain, and what you propose to preserve. I am applying for an industrial maintenance electrician role.
evals.expected_output: A source-preserving import workflow routed to the construction-trades-field-service domain, with an extraction report and confirmation before claims are rewritten.
assertions: The uploaded source is never overwritten.
Licenses, safety training, systems, environments, and verified scope are prioritized.
The candidate is asked to resolve uncertain extraction before finalization.

evals.prompt: Build a resume for a hotel front-desk supervisor applying to guest-services manager roles. I have experience with shift coverage, guest complaints, reservations, and training new hires, but I do not have reliable percentages.
evals.expected_output: A service-and-hospitality resume that uses verified scope and examples without fabricating satisfaction, revenue, or efficiency metrics.
assertions: The domain router selects retail-hospitality-service or explains a close alternative.
The draft can use counts, frequency, complexity, and examples when percentages are unavailable.
Guest recovery and team leadership evidence are visible.

evals.prompt: I work in a niche occupation that is not listed in your domain catalog. Help me create a resume from scratch without forcing me into the wrong industry template.
evals.expected_output: A general evidence-first fallback that asks about audience, outputs, constraints, tools, stakeholders, and outcomes, then allows the candidate to correct the inferred domain.
assertions: The workflow falls back to general rather than claiming a false match.
The candidate can override the router.
The resume is still evidence-based and target-specific.

evals.prompt: Redesign my uploaded product resume. It contains dates, percentages, project test counts, and several possible target roles. Keep this fast: confirm the important assumptions with me before generating any resume files, then build the final DOCX and PDF once.
evals.expected_output: The first build response presents a compact import and assumption brief, asks no more than three grouped confirmation questions, and does not render a labeled draft. After confirmation, it creates submission-ready files in one pass.
assertions: No DOCX or PDF is rendered before the candidate confirms material facts and target assumptions.
The confirmation request groups dates, metrics, ownership, target, contact details, and omissions into no more than three questions.
The normal post-confirmation output has no draft banner or draft filename.
